operators.formula_latex: {Cv}_{\tau} = \frac{\sum_{\substack{1 \leq \alpha \leq 3\\1 \leq i \leq N_{atoms}\\1 \leq t \leq n_{lag}}} {v}_{i,\alpha,\tau + t} {v}_{i,\alpha,t}}{N_{atoms} n_{lag}}
{M}_{\tau} = \frac{\sum_{\substack{1 \leq \alpha \leq 3\\1 \leq i \leq N_{atoms}\\1 \leq t \leq n_{lag}}} \left({r}_{i,\alpha,\tau + t} - {r}_{i,\alpha,t}\right)^{2}}{N_{atoms} n_{lag}}

interpretations: The four definitions transcribe the catalog formulas: origin sums over t = 1, ..., n_lag divided by N_atoms n_lag (velocity autocorrelation and mean squared displacement, summed over the three Cartesian components) or by n_lag (heat-current autocorrelation), and kappa_ab = V int_0^tau_max Jcorr_ab(tau) dtau/(k_B T^2). Records are functions of the integer sample index; the time step dt enters only through the position and Helfand-moment increments and the interpolant.

The theorems assume records periodic over the origin window, v(t + n_lag) = v(t) and J(t + n_lag) = J(t) (circular correlation, the periodic-padding assumption of FFT correlators), and integrated records advanced by dt times the sampled rate, r(t + 1) = r(t) + dt v(t) and G(t + 1) = G(t) + dt J(t). No statement is made about ensemble averages, ergodicity, finite-trajectory bias or convergence in the trajectory length.

Under these hypotheses the catalog's mean squared displacement is dt^2 [tau Cv(0) + 2 sum_{k=1}^{tau-1} (tau - k) Cv(k)] with Cv the catalog's velocity autocorrelation, so the Einstein and Green-Kubo diffusion estimators are one function of the trajectory.

The symmetrized Green-Kubo conductivity (kappa_ab + kappa_ba)/2 at tau_max = m dt, m >= 1, with the integral of the sampled autocorrelation taken as the integral of its piecewise-linear interpolant (the trapezoid rule on the samples 0, ..., m), equals the central-difference Einstein-Helfand estimator V (Lambda_ab(m + 1) - Lambda_ab(m - 1))/(4 k_B T^2 dt) with Lambda_ab(tau) = sum_t (G_a(t + tau) - G_a(t))(G_b(t + tau) - G_b(t))/n_lag. For a = b no symmetrization is needed.

The direct origin-averaged autocorrelation equals the inverse discrete Fourier transform of the cross spectrum conj(F J_a) F J_b/n_lag of one period, with F the unnormalized transform sum_j x_j exp(-2 pi i j k/n_lag) on Z/n_lag and F^-1 carrying the factor 1/n_lag: the FFT route of the catalog description.
